context.description: The encryption context: "default" sends {instance, purpose}; "off" sends none; an object is sent as is.

keyName.description: An alias such as alias/audit-seal (kms) or a transit key name. An ARN or a key id is refused.

keys.description: Where the keys live. Use `adapter` and a key by purpose (seal, pseudonym, conceal, archive), the shape of the storage port. `provider` is the first releases' shape (a pseudonymisation provider), deprecated. Unset, or provider `none`, means no pseudonyms, no key material and no resolve.

adapter.description: The key service: `kms` (AWS KMS, keys by alias), `transit` (OpenBAO) or `local` (a root file; development).

archive.description: The key the archive's objects are encrypted with (for S3, the SSE-KMS alias).

conceal.description: The key identities are sealed under, for the cases the law requires them to be recoverable.

instance.description: Names the installation in the default encryption context ({instance, purpose}), so a ciphertext made for one installation does not open as another's under a shared key. Bound into ciphertexts: choose something stable and non-secret.

dir.description: Where the wrapped data keys are kept. They are random, not derived, so this directory is the only copy; unset keeps them in memory, which a trial install may do and nothing else should.

rootFile.description: A file holding the 32-byte root the data keys are wrapped under.

provider.description: Deprecated: use `adapter`. `none`, `local` (a root and a directory) or `transit` (OpenBAO), with a key per tenant and purpose.

pseudonym.description: The key the per-tenant pseudonym secrets are wrapped under. Provisioned only for an installation that pseudonymises (the attested preset, or a profile that needs pseudonyms).

rootFile.description: The local adapter's root: a file of 32 bytes.

seal.description: The notary's seal key: asymmetric ECC P-384 (ES384). It signs; it takes no encryption context.

state.description: Where the wrapped per-tenant secrets behind the pseudonym purpose are kept, with the kms adapter: the installation's state store (SSM Parameter Store), under `root`/`address`. Nothing in it is usable without the pseudonym key.

address.description: The key below the root, for example internal/pseudonym.

root.description: The SSM path prefix of the installation, for example /audit/main.

prefix.description: What every key's name starts with: <prefix>.<purpose>.<tenant>.

openbao.description: How a process reaches an OpenBAO transit engine: where it is, and exactly one way of signing in.

caFile.description: A PEM bundle trusted beside the system roots, for a server on a private chain.

login.description: Sign in with a JWT: the pod's projected service-account token, presented to an auth mount. Nothing is stored.

jwtFile.description: The file holding the JWT, read at every login because the kubelet replaces a projected token before it expires.

mount.description: The JWT auth mount, for example jwt-devel.
Where the transit engine is mounted.

namespace.description: The OpenBAO namespace the engine and the auth mount are in. Unset is the root namespace.

tokenFile.description: A file holding a token, read on every call, for a token something else keeps renewed.

tokenSecret.description: The NAME of the secret holding a token, resolved through `secrets`.

postgres.description: A PostgreSQL connection. The URL carries no password: a password in it is refused, and `passwordSecret` names the secret that holds it.

secrets.description: Where a field named `...Secret` finds the secret it names. One source for the whole file: `env` (the name is an environment variable), `file` (the name is a path under `root`, one file per secret: a mounted Kubernetes Secret) or `ssm` (the name is a SecureString under `root` in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, read with the process's own identity). On AWS Lambda use `ssm`: the function's environment is never a place for a secret. Unset is `env`.

description: The configuration of audit-writer, the installation's front door and write path. Secrets are never in this file: a field named ...Secret holds the NAME of a secret, which the `secrets` block says how to find (an environment variable, a file or an SSM parameter). Telemetry is the OTEL_* environment, not configuration.

anonymousWrites.description: Accept writes over HTTP from callers nobody verified, stamped with no observer. For a trial install only.

apiVersion.description: The version of this document's shape, `audit.truvity.github.io/audit-writer/v2`. Absent means version 1, which is deprecated and read for one minor (`truvity.github.io/audit-writer/v1`); another value is refused, so that a later shape arrives by a version and not by a file that quietly means something else.

archive.description: What the process adds to the deployment's presets: where their static credentials are, and the default key.

ca.description: A bundle of certificate authorities, for a store whose certificate is not signed by a public root.

kmsKey.description: The key objects are encrypted with where a preset names no `key_alias` of its own. Unset uses the bucket's default encryption, which a deployment should still be setting.

stateRoot.description: The root of the installation's state store (SSM Parameter Store, through the storage port), for example /audit/main. A preset's `credentials` address in the deployment document is read below it with the process's own identity: the value is a JSON object {accessKeyID, secretAccessKey}. No secret is in this file. Needed when a preset names `credentials`.

catalogues.description: A directory of catalogues to register at start-up.

consume.description: What a writer reads its records from, beside its own sink: exactly one of `nats` and `sqs`.

nats.description: A NATS JetStream stream; what `stream` says.

ackWait.description: How long the stream waits for a batch to be taken before offering it again. It must exceed `roll.interval` plus the longest a put can take.

batch.description: How many records are taken from the stream at once.

consumer.description: The durable consumer this installation's writers share.

sqs.description: An SQS queue the writer consumes. Credentials are never in the file: the process uses the SDK's ambient ones, which on Kubernetes is the pod's workload identity (EKS Pod Identity or IRSA) bound through the service account.

batch.description: How many messages are received at once, one to ten.

fifo.description: The queue is FIFO. It must agree with the URL, which ends in `.fifo` for one. A FIFO queue absorbs a repeated record itself, inside its five-minute window; a standard queue relies on the writer's deduplication.

region.description: The queue's region. Unset is the SDK's: AWS_REGION, which EKS Pod Identity and IRSA set.

visibility.description: How long a received message is hidden from other consumers while the writer writes it. It must outlast the write, or the message is delivered twice.

database.description: The shared deduplication table and the catalogue registry, as the writer's own database role: it holds those and none of the index, which audit-observe writes. Without it the writer deduplicates in process and may only run one replica.

deployment.description: Path to the profile configuration: which framework profiles each profile is composed from.

forgetIdentities.description: Do not keep the identity behind each pseudonym, sealed under its key. By default it is kept, so that resolve can find it.

forward.description: Where a receiver sends what it took: exactly one of `nats`, `sqs` and `log`. `log` is allowed only with `require: logged`.

log.description: The log sink: one JSON line per record on standard output, which survives nothing but the log pipeline. Nothing to configure.

nats.description: A NATS JetStream stream; what `stream` says.

ackWait.description: How long the stream waits for a batch to be taken before offering it again. It must exceed `roll.interval` plus the longest a put can take.

batch.description: How many records are taken from the stream at once.

consumer.description: The durable consumer this installation's writers share.

sqs.description: An SQS queue the receiver publishes to. Credentials are never in the file: the process uses the SDK's ambient ones, which on Kubernetes is the pod's workload identity (EKS Pod Identity or IRSA) bound through the service account.

fifo.description: The queue is FIFO. It must agree with the URL, which ends in `.fifo` for one. A FIFO queue absorbs a repeated record itself, inside its five-minute window; a standard queue relies on the writer's deduplication.

region.description: The queue's region. Unset is the SDK's: AWS_REGION, which EKS Pod Identity and IRSA set.

mode.description: `writer` serves the sink, writes the archive and consumes the stream when there is one. `receiver` serves the sink and publishes to the stream and nothing else: it holds no archive and no keys, because a receiver holding either would be a writer.

replicas.description: How many writers share this stream. Above one it needs a database, and with local keys a directory every replica shares.

require.description: The weakest durability this process's chain may give. Unset is `archived` for a writer and `queued` for a receiver. At start-up the process refuses to run if what it is configured with can never give that: a receiver, which holds no archive, cannot promise `archived`, and `forward.log` cannot promise more than `logged`. A write acknowledged weaker than this fails. See ADR 0059.

roll.description: How much a writer gathers from the stream before it writes, which decides how many objects a day of records becomes.

interval.description: How long gathered records wait before they are written, and how long an object stays open within one write.

maxRecords.description: How many gathered records are written at once.

stream.description: The wide stream, as the NATS shorthand: for a receiver it is `forward.nats`, for a writer `consume.nats`. Give it or the longhand, not both.

ackWait.description: How long the stream waits for a batch to be taken before offering it again. It must exceed `roll.interval` plus the longest a put can take.

batch.description: How many records are taken from the stream at once.

consumer.description: The durable consumer this installation's writers share.

workloads.description: Path to the file naming the issuers trusted to say which workload is publishing, and which source each speaks for. Exactly one of `workloads` and `anonymousWrites`.

title: audit-writer
